requirement.original: Fix MCP title change -- the tool call still fails with 'endpoint connection error' even after hook exemption was added
requirement.clarified: Apply the per-request StreamableHTTPServerTransport pattern from worktree commit 0fd4112f to the production startHappyServer.ts at /root/happy, fixing the stateless transport reuse guard in MCP SDK 1.27.1
requirement.what: Fix startHappyServer.ts to create fresh McpServer + StreamableHTTPServerTransport per HTTP request instead of reusing a single instance
requirement.why: MCP SDK 1.27.1 added a guard that throws 'Stateless transport cannot be reused across requests' when sessionIdGenerator is undefined and the transport handles a second request. The production code uses the old single-transport pattern, causing every change_title call to fail with HTTP 500.

included: Apply persistTitle metadata-await fix from worktree
excluded: UI rendering changes for change_title tool

success_criteria: HTTP MCP server returns 200 for initialize + tools/call sequence
Bridge process can connect and call change_title without 'endpoint connection error'
Multiple sequential change_title calls all succeed
Session title updates in server metadata (summary field)
constraints: Must work with MCP SDK 1.27.1 (current production version)
Must not change the bridge process
Daemon restart required after CLI rebuild

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Claude reports 'endpoint connection error' when calling mcp__happy__change_title. Bridge logs show 'Streamable HTTP error: Error POSTing to endpoint:'. HTTP MCP server at port 46835 returns 500 for ALL requests.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: MCP SDK 1.27.1 WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.handleRequest() (line 139-141 of webStandardStreamableHttp.js) throws 'Stateless transport cannot be reused across requests' when sessionIdGenerator is undefined and _hasHandledRequest is true. Production startHappyServer.ts creates ONE transport at startup and reuses it, hitting this guard on the second request. The error is caught by @hono/node-server's getRequestListener which returns HTTP 500 silently -- the outer try-catch never sees it, so nothing is logged.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A - SDK behavior change in @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.27.1; fix exists as 0fd4112f in worktree but not applied to production
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: The old startHappyServer pattern (single transport) worked with MCP SDK < 1.27. When the SDK was updated to 1.27.1 (which added the _hasHandledRequest guard for stateless transports), the old pattern broke. The fix was developed (commit 0fd4112f) but only applied in the worktree, never merged to production /root/happy.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Every HTTP request after the first one to the MCP server throws, making the change_title tool permanently broken. The error is swallowed by @hono/node-server so nothing appears in logs, making debugging extremely difficult.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: SDK 1.27.1 installed -> startHappyServer creates single transport -> first bridge request succeeds (_hasHandledRequest set to true) -> all subsequent requests throw -> bridge reports 'Error POSTing to endpoint' -> Claude reports 'endpoint connection error'

context.codebase_state: Production code at /root/happy has old pattern. Fix exists at worktree 0fd4112f. Running process (PID 2025675) uses old compiled code.
context.recent_commits: 0fd4112f (worktree only): fix MCP server broken by SDK 1.27 transport reuse rejection

development_approach.strategy: Copy the fixed startHappyServer.ts from the worktree to the production repo, rebuild, and reinstall. The worktree version creates a fresh McpServer + StreamableHTTPServerTransport per HTTP request, avoiding the _hasHandledRequest guard.
development_approach.validation_approach: 1. After rebuild, start a test HTTP MCP server with the fixed code. 2. Use StreamableHTTPClientTransport to connect, initialize, and call change_title. 3. Verify HTTP 200 on all requests. 4. Restart dev daemon and verify Claude can call change_title successfully.

research_findings.reason: Root cause identified through runtime debugging (node inspector CDP). No external research needed -- the fix already exists in the codebase (commit 0fd4112f).

investigation_evidence.debugger_finding: Node.js CDP debugger confirmed: process pauses at webStandardStreamableHttp.js:140 (handleRequest) on every request to port 46835. The throw is 'Stateless transport cannot be reused across requests.'
investigation_evidence.http_test: curl to port 46835 returns HTTP 500 with empty body for ALL request types (POST, GET, DELETE)
investigation_evidence.bridge_error: StreamableHTTPClientTransport.connect() throws 'Streamable HTTP error: Error POSTing to endpoint:' when connecting to port 46835
investigation_evidence.standalone_test: Fresh MCP server with per-request transport pattern works perfectly (HTTP 200)
investigation_evidence.no_log_explanation: @hono/node-server's getRequestListener catches the error internally and writes HTTP 500 before the await in StreamableHTTPServerTransport.handleRequest resolves, so the outer try-catch never fires
